news.headline: Cafe owner’s death: Model Shraddha Dubey, 2 others sent to UP on transit remand
news.story_lead: Cafe owner’s death: Model Shraddha Dubey, 2 others sent to UP on transit remand The UP STF team left with Shraddha Dubey, her sister and driver for Lucknow, 900 km away, by road after the Nagpur court order. An Uttar Pradesh police team left for Lucknow on Wednesday afternoon after a Nagpur court granted transit remand for model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, 31, her sister Rashmi Dubey and their driver Tanveer Ali alias Danish. The three were arrested in Nagpur on Tuesday in connection with the murder of cafe owner Shiva Sharma, 28, who died after falling from an apartment building in Lucknow on October 9.
news.full_article_text: Cafe owner’s death: Model Shraddha Dubey, 2 others sent to UP on transit remand The UP STF team left with Shraddha Dubey, her sister and driver for Lucknow, 900 km away, by road after the Nagpur court order. An Uttar Pradesh police team left for Lucknow on Wednesday afternoon after a Nagpur court granted transit remand for model and social media influencer Shraddha Dubey, 31, her sister Rashmi Dubey and their driver Tanveer Ali alias Danish. The three were arrested in Nagpur on Tuesday in connection with the murder of cafe owner Shiva Sharma, 28, who died after falling from an apartment building in Lucknow on October 9. A Nagpur crime branch team led by senior police inspector Shubhangi Deshmukh and UP special task force (STF) officers produced the three before Chief Judicial Magistrate Sameer Sattaram Kamat at about 2:30pm. The judge granted transit remand to the UP team till October 24. The STF team left for Lucknow, 900 km away, by road after the court order. Deep Dive Shraddha Dubey, her sister and their driver, who were on the run, had travelled to Kanpur, Agra and Nepal before landing in Maharashtra. They arrived in Nagpur on Monday and rented a flat on the 11th floor of an apartment in the Beltarodi area of south-west Nagpur. The three were tracked down by the Nagpur crime branch on a tip from the UP police using CCTV footage, local intelligence, and a crucial tip from an e-rickshaw driver who gave the burqa-clad suspects a ride, Sharma, who is alleged to be Shraddha’s live-in partner, died after falling from the fourth floor. The incident was initially treated as an accidental death, but his mother later lodged a murder complaint alleging that her son had been subjected to physical and mental torture. She told police that Sharma called her shortly before his death and said he would return in five minutes after Shraddha called him outside. A murder case was registered on October 10. The case gained further attention after videos of Shraddha surfaced on social media. In a video interview to a news agency, she denied any role in Sharma’s death and claimed he died by suicide due to financial difficulties. She alleged that Sharma owed between ₹ 15 lakh and ₹ 20 lakh and had threatened to end his life if he could not repay the money.

news.story_lead: Jeweller who crafted 'Sengol' installed in Parliament dies at 99. PM Modi condoles loss Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers. India's leading jeweller Vummidi Ethiraj passed away in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on Wednesday at the age of 99.
news.full_article_text: Jeweller who crafted 'Sengol' installed in Parliament dies at 99. PM Modi condoles loss Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers. India's leading jeweller Vummidi Ethiraj passed away in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, on Wednesday at the age of 99. Following his demise, Vice President CP Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed deep sadness and condoled his death. PM Modi paid tribute to Ethiraj in a post on X, noting that he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the Sengol that was presented to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The PM said, "Deeply saddened by the passing of Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji. Hailing from a distinguished family based in Tamil Nadu, he will always be remembered for his efforts in crafting the historic Sengol that was presented to Former Prime Minister Nehru." PM Modi said that many years later, in 2023, it was this government which had the honour of giving the 'Sengol' a place of pride in the new Parliament building. "Many years later, in 2023, it was our Government which had the honour of giving the Sengol a place of pride in the new Parliament building. During that time, I had the honour of meeting Thiru Vummidi Ethiraj Ji and expressing gratitude for what he has done for our nation and culture. His life and craftsmanship represent a remarkable connection between India's glorious traditions and our national journey. My heartfelt condolences to his family and admirers. Om Shanti," the prime minister added. Also Read | Murugan’s resignation letter: Praise for Modi’s Tamil outreach, from Sitharaman and Jaishankar to Thirukkural and Sengol Condoling the death in a post on X, Vice President Radhakrishnan said he was "deeply saddened" by the demise of Ethiraj, "whose efforts in crafting the historic Sengol, a sacred symbol of India’s civilisational heritage, will always be remembered with respect and gratitude." "His invaluable contribution to preserving India’s rich tradition of jewellery craftsmanship leaves behind an enduring legacy. My heartfelt condolences to his family and loved ones," he added. Also Read | What is ‘Sengol’, whose installation in new Parliament triggered row? Who was Vummidi Ethiraj? Ethiraj was the patriarch of the Vummidi family that owns the 125-year-old Vummidi Bangaru Jewellers, according to news agency PTI . Ethiraj worked on the creation of Sengol, the gold-plated silver sceptre, symbolising the handover of power from British authorities to independent India in 1947. On the eve of Independence, Nehru received the Sengol from the Adheenams (priests) of the Thiruvaduthurai Adheenam (Mutt) in Tamil Nadu, who travelled specially for the occasion, the report added. Decades later, the Sengol found a place of prominence in the new Parliament building. Crafted by Vummidi Jewellers, the Sengol was ceremonially installed in the new Parliament building by Prime Minister Modi on May 28, 2023. news.exam_corner_topic: USGS Landsat Science Team Focuses on Advanced Satellite Technology

news.headline: USGS Landsat Science Team Directs Focus Towards Advanced Satellite Technology
news.story_lead: The United States Geological Survey (USGS) Landsat Science Team is focusing its research and technical efforts on advanced satellite technology. This initiative aims to enhance Earth observation capabilities, data precision, and remote sensing applications for environmental monitoring.
news.full_article_text:
### USGS Landsat Science Team Focuses on Advanced Satellite Technology

The United States Geological Survey (USGS) Landsat Science Team is prioritizing advanced satellite technology to modernise Earth observation and remote sensing infrastructure. The initiative focuses on evaluating next-generation satellite sensor capabilities and data processing methods.

### Key Factual Highlights
* **Organising Entity:** United States Geological Survey (USGS) Landsat Science Team.
* **Core Focus Area:** Advanced satellite technology, high-resolution remote sensing, and Earth observation system enhancements.
* **Primary Objective:** Improving the quality, spectral resolution, and continuity of space-based land monitoring data for global scientific and policy applications.
bullet_points: The USGS Landsat Science Team is focusing efforts on advanced satellite technology.
The primary aim is to modernize satellite sensors and remote sensing data collection.
The Landsat program is jointly managed by NASA (satellite design/launch) and the USGS (data archive/distribution).
Advanced satellite capabilities will support enhanced monitoring of Earth's land surface, vegetation, and natural resources.
key_facts: Entity involved: USGS Landsat Science Team.
Primary domain: Advanced satellite technology and satellite-based Earth observation.
Managing Agency: United States Geological Survey (USGS).
important_dates: 2026-10-20: Announcement date regarding the USGS Landsat Science Team's focus on advanced satellite technology.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Science & Technology - Space technology, remote sensing satellites, Earth observation programs (Landsat).
Mains: GS Paper III - Technological developments in space, applications of satellite remote sensing in resource mapping and environmental monitoring.
news.upsc_analysis: The focus on advanced satellite technology by the USGS Landsat Science Team underscores the critical role of continuous technical upgrading in remote sensing. High-resolution land monitoring is essential for addressing global environmental challenges, land-use planning, and disaster assessment.
causes: Evolution of remote sensing requirements requiring modern satellite sensor technology.
impacts: Enhanced precision and scientific utility of satellite imagery for global Earth surface tracking.
challenges: Integrating advanced satellite sensor hardware while ensuring seamless historical continuity with legacy Landsat datasets.
government_steps: Strategic planning and scientific evaluation conducted by the USGS Landsat Science Team.
way_forward: Strengthening joint technical collaborations between space agencies and scientific research teams to deploy cutting-edge Earth observation satellites.
news.mains_notes: The Landsat Science Team's focus on advanced satellite technology highlights the significance of spaceborne remote sensing in Earth observation. Continuous innovation in sensor resolution and data processing ensures accurate natural resource management and environmental change tracking globally.
mains_questions: Discuss the role of Earth observation satellite programs like Landsat in natural resource management and environmental monitoring.
How do advances in satellite remote sensing technology enhance climate change observation and disaster risk reduction?
news.takeaway: The USGS Landsat Science Team is prioritizing advanced satellite technology to enhance global remote sensing and Earth observation capabilities.
prelims_facts: The Landsat program is a joint initiative between NASA and the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).
Landsat represents the longest continuous spaceborne Earth observation archive, running since 1972.

news.headline: With Marco Rubio in India, Trump says trade deal ‘pretty close’, hints at ‘different kind of deal’
news.story_lead: With Marco Rubio in India, Trump says trade pact ‘pretty close’, hints at ‘different kind of deal’ US secretary of state Marco Rubio too had, on Tuesday, said that India and the US are “very, very close” to finalising a trade agreement. United States President Donald Trump has said that New Delhi and Washington are “pretty close” to finalising a trade deal, even as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is in India on a three-day official visit. “They want to make a deal.
news.full_article_text: With Marco Rubio in India, Trump says trade pact ‘pretty close’, hints at ‘different kind of deal’ US secretary of state Marco Rubio too had, on Tuesday, said that India and the US are “very, very close” to finalising a trade agreement. United States President Donald Trump has said that New Delhi and Washington are “pretty close” to finalising a trade deal, even as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is in India on a three-day official visit. “They want to make a deal. We’re going to make a deal. Pretty close, yeah,” Bloomberg cited Trump as saying on Tuesday, while speaking to reporters at the White House. The US President further said it “could be a much different kind of deal”, but did not elaborate further. Trump's remarks follow optimistic statements made by both Indian and US leaders in the recent past regarding the prospects of the trade deal. New Delhi and Washington had announced the framework for an interim trade agreement in February earlier this year. ‘Very close, some items left’: Rubio on trade deal Deep Dive Rubio too had, on Tuesday, said that India and the US are “very, very close” to finalising a trade agreement. “The State Department doesn't negotiate trade agreements, but we are very much involved in what's happening...We're very, very close. I would say we're about as close as you can be without having executed the agreement,” he said during his second official visit to India. He said there are a “small number of items left to wrap up”, adding that these too would be dealt with “shortly”. Rubio expressed hope that there would be “good news to announce soon”, while saying he was optimistic that both sides will have “something in place”. Rubio met external affairs minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday, wherein he urged New Delhi to increase energy trade and step up purchases of American technologies and systems. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor also said, last week at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, that the “the big items are done”, and that the two countries are very close to “landing it.” Rubio suggests trade deal ‘considered’ ahead of Russian energy waivers Ahead of his India visit as well, Rubio had in Uzbekistan said that Washington was “very close” to finalising a trade deal with India, adding that it was one of the things taken into consideration when making decisions on national security waivers. “We're trying to finalise a trade deal with India right now. We're very close to doing that. So that's one of the things we take into consideration when the President makes a decision about national security waivers and things of that nature,” Rubio said while speaking to reporters in Samarkand. Also Read | Trump's Russia oil tariff waiver, the midterm election calculus behind it and the stakes for India-US trade deal The remarks came days after US President Donald Trump waived some sanctions related to Russian energy under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act citing “national security” reasons. The law, which has been put on hold, would have imposed tariffs of up to 100 per cent on top five purchasers of Russian crude oil or gas, which included India. To be sure, the secondary sanctions have just been deferred, leaving Trump free to use the law against these countries whenever he chooses. Union minister Piyush Goyal says first tranche of trade deal finalised Union minister Piyush Goyal had, last week, said the first tranche of India-US bilateral trade agreement is ready and legal drafting is currently under process. “The US bilateral trade agreement's first tranche has been finalised. It's going through the final contours, the legal drafting, and we hope to be able to finalize that soon and operationalise it once we get a comparable or competitive advantage over our peer countries,” he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arya Mishra Arya Mishra is a Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, and a key member of the digital news team focusing on urgent breaking developments across India and the world. With a sharp editorial instinct and strong reporting skills, Arya covers high-impact crime incidents, public safety and justice issues, political developments, education policy and international affairs, consistently delivering clear, accurate and timely journalism. Her recent reporting highlights include detailed coverage of serious criminal cases, politics as well as analyses of national education reforms and international diplomatic moves. On the world news front, she has written about global trade policy changes and security developments, including tariff shifts by the United States and strategic counter-terrorism strategies being rolled out by Ministry of Home Affairs. Arya thrives in fast-paced environments – running live blogs, crafting in-depth explainers and real-time news coverage that keeps readers informed as stories evolve. Before joining Hindustan Times, she was a part of The Indian Express online team. Outside the newsroom, she is an avid reader, with a love for thriller and suspense fiction, and enjoys music as a way to unwind. With more than three years of experience in dynamic newsrooms, Arya brings curiosity, clarity and commitment to every story she covers. Read More

news.headline: 'Tired of spreading lies': BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi over foreign trip; Cong hits out
news.story_lead: 'Tired of spreading lies': BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi over foreign trip; Cong hits out BJP leader Shazia Ilmi also questioned Gandhi’s commitment, accusing him of using political protests as an excuse for taking another break. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has taken a swipe at Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his purported ongoing foreign trip, saying the Congress leader is “tired of spreading lies” after his campaign against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, even as the Opposition said all protests have been put on hold in view of the festive season. Taking to X, the BJP shared a purported video of Gandhi seated inside a business-class cabin of a flight.
news.full_article_text: 'Tired of spreading lies': BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi over foreign trip; Cong hits out BJP leader Shazia Ilmi also questioned Gandhi’s commitment, accusing him of using political protests as an excuse for taking another break. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has taken a swipe at Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his purported ongoing foreign trip, saying the Congress leader is “tired of spreading lies” after his campaign against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, even as the Opposition said all protests have been put on hold in view of the festive season. Taking to X, the BJP shared a purported video of Gandhi seated inside a business-class cabin of a flight. “I’m tired of spreading lies… Let me go roam around Vietnam for a few days… Who would even find out?” it said. The INDIA bloc has been seeking Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and even held a series of protests in recent days. Gandhi was at the forefront of the protests and marches in Delhi, even as he and several other leaders were detained on several occasions. The purported tour also comes after Gandhi’s participation in the Congress’s Goa Rakhon Yatra in the poll-bound state. According to reports, he is expected to be away for four days. BJP spokesperson RP Singh accused Gandhi of repeatedly going abroad after participating in political campaigns. “After undertaking a yatra in Bihar, he went abroad on a holiday for two months,” he said, suggesting that the latest trip followed a familiar pattern. The Congress dismissed the BJP’s criticism as an unnecessary controversy. “He is merely stepping away for two or three days; what is the problem with that? The INDIA bloc will stage a massive protest against Gyanesh Kumar on November 1st,” Congress general secretary KC Venugopal told a Malayalam news channel. Former Congress MP Sandeep Dikshit said Gandhi’s foreign visits often involved interactions with students and intellectuals, and questioned why the BJP was making an issue of the trip. Dikshit also cited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s foreign visits, arguing that the same scrutiny was not applied to his travel. Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said, ”Regime change will happen… Rahul Gandhi has gone to Vietnam. Let him return; it will happen!" The BJP has often been critical of Gandhi’s frequent foreign tours. While debating on a bill to remove Special Protection Group (SPG) cover from the Gandhi family in 2019, Union home minister Amit Shah said Gandhi travelled abroad 156 times, of which 143 were made without SPG cover. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Saubhadra Chatterji Saubhadra Chatterji is Deputy Political Editor at the Hindustan Times. He writes on both politics and policies.

news.headline: ‘No safe havens for terrorists’: With Pakistan minister in audience, Rajnath Singh calls out terror backers
news.story_lead: ‘No safe havens for terrorists’: With Pakistan minister in audience, Rajnath Singh calls out terror backers India reiterated its opposition to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, citing concerns over the route passing through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday called for joint action to dismantle terrorism, asserting that there can be no justification for the scourge or double standards in tackling it, in a pointed message delivered in the presence of Pakistan’s deputy prime minister and defence minister Ishaq Dar at the 25th meeting of SCO council of heads of government at Dushanbe in Tajikistan . “Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce.
news.full_article_text: ‘No safe havens for terrorists’: With Pakistan minister in audience, Rajnath Singh calls out terror backers India reiterated its opposition to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, citing concerns over the route passing through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Tuesday called for joint action to dismantle terrorism, asserting that there can be no justification for the scourge or double standards in tackling it, in a pointed message delivered in the presence of Pakistan’s deputy prime minister and defence minister Ishaq Dar at the 25th meeting of SCO council of heads of government at Dushanbe in Tajikistan . “Terrorism results in the loss of innocent lives and disrupts investment and commerce. It radicalises societies and deprives youth of the opportunities they rightfully deserve. There can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in addressing it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to terrorists,” Singh said in a thinly veiled swipe at Pakistan . Also read: Ecosystem of terrorism must be firmly and collectively 'dismantled': Rajnath Singh at SCO meet Singh calls for dismantling the entire terror ecosystem Terrorism, Singh said, poses a grave threat to peace and development, and its entire ecosystem must be collectively dismantled. India and Pakistan joined the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation as members in June 2017. In his address, he stressed that connectivity must be based on “consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity” of all countries, arguing that “projects not founded on these principles will not be sustainable.” The comments are significant because New Delhi has long opposed the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) , a flagship project under China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), as a key section of the corridor passes through Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK). In the past, India has expressed concern at China and Pakistan using CPEC to alter the status quo in the region, and said the connectivity project passes through Indian territory that is under “forcible occupation” by Pakistan. Chinese Premier Li Qiang also attended the SCO meeting. Also read: Future military power will depend on decision-making speed, not platform numbers: Rajnath Singh India backs trade corridors linking Central Asia with wider markets “Connectivity is crucial for our shared prosperity. India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new avenues for development. Initiatives such as the International North-South Transport Corridor and the Chabahar Port can contribute significantly to connecting Central Asia with broader markets,” he said. Singh also highlighted the need to move beyond physical connectivity by simplifying customs procedures, promoting digital documentation, improving logistics and adopting interoperable digital solutions to reduce the cost of doing business across the region. Economic engagement must be inclusive and mutually beneficial for all member states, he said. “India believes that the SCO must remain efficient and steadfast in its adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, consensus, and mutual respect. New mechanisms should focus on clearly identified needs, avoid duplication, and prioritise delivering practical value to Member States.” Also read: Rajnath Singh signals push for deeper military ties with ASEAN, offers radars, air defence systems Singh flags geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions Singh said the SCO must build consensus and translate it into concrete action to address the uncertain global economic environment marked by geopolitical tensions, disruptions to trade and supply chains, concerns over energy and food security, and emerging technological divides. There is a need to strengthen supply chains, facilitate trade and investment, and leverage technology to drive development, he said. The meeting reviewed progress in multilateral economic and trade cooperation among SCO Member States and discussed measures to further strengthen cooperation in areas such as transport, finance, digital economy and social development, the defence ministry said in a statement. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rahul Singh Rahul Singh is Defence Editor at Hindustan Times and has covered military affairs and national security for nearly 25 years. Apart from extensive and deep reporting on the Indian military, including several newsbreaks that have set the national news agenda over the years, Rahul has reported from conflict zones including Jammu & Kashmir, India’s North-east and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Rahul has co-authored the bestselling 'India's Most Fearless' series of books on recent Indian military operations. Widely read and translated into multiple languages, the books place an emphasis on firsthand accounts of daring missions across the three services. His work has been adapted into web series and films including the National Award-winning Amaran. Rahul comes from an Army background and attended schools across the country before completing his education from Panjab University, Chandigarh. Grew up playing tennis, now mostly cheers from the sidelines. Works in Delhi, heart in the mountains. Read More

news.headline: Rubio says US immigration curbs not aimed at India, blames 'mass migration' for visa crackdown
news.story_lead: Rubio says US immigration curbs not aimed at India, blames 'mass migration' for visa crackdown Rubio's remarks come amid concerns in India over the Trump administration's tougher approach to immigration, including restrictions affecting work visas. US secretary of state Marco Rubio has sought to allay Indian concerns over Washington's tightening of immigration rules, saying the changes are part of a global effort to overhaul the American immigration system and are not targeted at India, despite their impact on Indian students and skilled professionals. “From your perspective here in India, it may seem targeted at India, (but) it’s not,” Rubio told The Indian Express in an interview.
news.full_article_text: Rubio says US immigration curbs not aimed at India, blames 'mass migration' for visa crackdown Rubio's remarks come amid concerns in India over the Trump administration's tougher approach to immigration, including restrictions affecting work visas. US secretary of state Marco Rubio has sought to allay Indian concerns over Washington's tightening of immigration rules, saying the changes are part of a global effort to overhaul the American immigration system and are not targeted at India, despite their impact on Indian students and skilled professionals. “From your perspective here in India, it may seem targeted at India, (but) it’s not,” Rubio told The Indian Express in an interview. He said the Donald Trump administration was attempting to address what it viewed as years of neglect of the immigration system and alleged misuse of visa programmes. “The biggest threat to legal immigration is illegal immigration. The biggest threat to legal immigration is mass migration,” Rubio said, adding that the latter was “not an Indian phenomenon” but was more closely associated with other parts of the world. His remarks come amid concerns in India over the Trump administration's tougher approach to immigration, including restrictions affecting work visas and the scrutiny faced by foreign students and skilled professionals seeking to enter the US. The changes have raised questions about the future of opportunities for Indians, who form a significant share of applicants for several American visa categories. Rubio, however, said Washington continued to welcome people seeking to visit, study, work and invest in the US, provided they complied with the country’s immigration laws. “We want people to visit the United States. We want people to study in the United States. There are certain people that we want, that want to come work for a time in the United States. We want people to invest in the United States,” he said in the interview. “But we want it done through a system of laws that are complied with,” he added. 'Fixing' immigration system Explaining the administration's approach, Rubio said the US was seeking to address what it considered longstanding problems in its immigration framework. He alleged that 20 million people had entered the country unlawfully during Joe Biden's four-year presidency and said several visa programmes had been abused. “Again, it is not unique to Indians or India,” he said, citing birth tourism as another example of practices the administration was seeking to address. Rubio acknowledged that the impact of the changes could appear disproportionately large in India because of the extensive economic and people-to-people ties between the two countries, as well as the number of Indians applying under particular visa categories. “Because of the developments, because of the ties between our countries, because of how developed your economy is, there are certain categories of visas that see a large number of Indians applying for,” he told Indian Express. The US, he added, was seeking to build an immigration system that would be sustainable over the long term. Once the system was fixed, he argued, it could ultimately benefit people using the programmes while serving American interests. “There is virtually no country on Earth that I visit where I don’t get a complaint about some visa or process, because we are fixing it globally,” Rubio said. India-US look to bolster ties The remarks come as New Delhi and Washington seek to maintain momentum in bilateral ties despite differences over trade, tariffs and energy relations. In the interview, the US secretary of state described the relationship as positive and said it had become a feature of American foreign policy. He said the two countries were close to finalising a trade agreement, with 99% of the work completed and only weeks, rather than months, remaining to conclude it. Trade tensions have been a source of friction, with the Trump administration's tariff measures and its approach to India's purchases of Russian oil adding to uncertainty in bilateral economic relations. Rubio said the tariffs were not intended to punish or harm India, arguing that Washington was attempting to balance its foreign policy objectives with the need to preserve important partnerships. He also sought to reassure New Delhi over Washington’s engagement with Pakistan, saying the US relationship with no country would come at the expense of its ties with India. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: Social media influencer with 1.4 mn followers found dead in Chennai; suicide suspected
news.story_lead: Social media influencer with 1.4 mn followers found dead in Chennai; suicide suspected In one of the last videos uploaded by him, he is seen claiming that he was upset after a complaint was filed against him with the regulator body SEBI. A social media influencer with over 1.4 million followers was found dead at his Chennai home on Tuesday night as police suspect it as a case of suicide. Police said the victim allegedly died by suicide at his residence in the city as he was targeted for offering financial advises without the license from capital market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
news.full_article_text: Social media influencer with 1.4 mn followers found dead in Chennai; suicide suspected In one of the last videos uploaded by him, he is seen claiming that he was upset after a complaint was filed against him with the regulator body SEBI. A social media influencer with over 1.4 million followers was found dead at his Chennai home on Tuesday night as police suspect it as a case of suicide. Police said the victim allegedly died by suicide at his residence in the city as he was targeted for offering financial advises without the license from capital market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The victim was known for his various videos on social media channels Instagram, YouTube offering financial advice to people in Tamil explaining about making investments in various financial instruments including mutual funds, trading among many others. According to his close friends, he has been engaged in this work over the last five years and has garnered over 1.4 million followers. Also Read: 23-year-old man stabs woman, her mother before dying by suicide in Jalandhar “A resident of Kanathur located on the East Coast Road near Chennai, the influencer allegedly died by suicide late on Tuesday”, police said. The body was recovered from his house at Kanathur and has been sent to the district government hospital for an autopsy, police said. What he said in a recent video “I have been doing this for the last five years and they (cyber bullying) are allegedly threatening my family by saying I know this chief minister, I know this lawmaker. I can remove all your videos”, he is seen claiming in his video stating that he was ‘mentally harassed’ through the cyber bullying allegedly they were unhappy with his growth. His work has also received a couple of recognitions including being the recipient of the ‘Best Finance Channel’ constituted by the city-based private entity in 2025. Reacting to his death, other social media influencers expressed their condolences. Prawin Ganeshan, a social media user said, “Deeply saddened by reports that the influencer has died by suicide. RIP”. Another social media user Kirubakaran Rajendran said, “(The owner of YouTube channel) with 1.3 million followers on Instagram, one of the biggest finance creators in Tamil Nadu. Gone. I did not know him personally, but I know this world.” Recently, the social media account of Harish on Instagram was removed by Meta Inc as the influencer has been giving financial advice to the members of public without the mandatory recognition from SEBI. Rajendran further said, “From what I understand, his Instagram account was recently taken down by Meta. For a creator that is a huge blow. That is losing years of work, your income, your community and your routine, all gone. Nobody around you fully understands what that does to your head.” Another social media user Kishore K Swamy said, “The YouTube channel chap has taken the extreme step of suicide allegedly because of cyber bullying by another youtuber (Jason Samuel) the CEO of venture studio Zemuria Inc.” Also Read: Haryanvi wrestler dies by suicide Responding to the comment of Swamy, Jason Samuel said, he was deeply saddened, heavily grieving, shocked and frozen at what had happened. In his official social media account on Wednesday, Samuel said, “I have not cyber-bullied him. I pointed out his lack of license and authority, misrepresentation of licence and fraud on SEBI and AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) where has not got SEBI RIA (SEBI Registered Investment Advisor) for his work and misrepresented that he had an AMFI license when he got the ARN only recently i.e., illegal activity”. Samuel further said, “I asked him in the video to come back and do this with a proper SEBI license. I never intended or expected this drastic measure to happen and I mourn the loss”. Meanwhile, a case was yet to be registered over the death of the social media influencer by the local police. news.headline: Maternity leave amendment followed women manufacturing employment decline: Study
news.story_lead: Women manufacturing employment decline followed maternity leave amendment: Study The researchers recommended shifting maternity leave financing from individual employers to social insurance The 2017 amendment, which provided for increased paid maternity leave from 12 weeks to 26 weeks for the first two children, followed an 8.4% decline in women’s employment and a 2.6% rise in men’s employment at covered manufacturing firms, according to a study. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, mandated employers to bear the cost of the leave. It changed the provisions of an over 55-year-old law, entitling women employees to certain benefits.
news.full_article_text: Women manufacturing employment decline followed maternity leave amendment: Study The researchers recommended shifting maternity leave financing from individual employers to social insurance The 2017 amendment, which provided for increased paid maternity leave from 12 weeks to 26 weeks for the first two children, followed an 8.4% decline in women’s employment and a 2.6% rise in men’s employment at covered manufacturing firms, according to a study. The Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, mandated employers to bear the cost of the leave. It changed the provisions of an over 55-year-old law, entitling women employees to certain benefits. The new law made it mandatory for every establishment with 50 or more employees to have the facility of a creche within a prescribed distance. The employers were bound to allow a woman employee four visits a day to the creche. The study, ‘Mandated Maternity Leave and Labour Substitution: Firm-Level Evidence from India’, found that the number of days women worked fell by 9.5%. The number of days men worked rose by 2.1%. The study was published in August as part of the IZA Discussion Paper Series by IZA@LISER Network, a global community of over 2,000 labour economics scholars across more than 450 institutions. The Luxembourg Institute of Socio-Economic Research coordinates the network The researchers, Souvik Banerjee, Preeti Jaiswal (IIT Bombay), and Sankar Mukhopadhyay of the University of Nevada, Reno, and IZA@LISER, used Annual Survey of Industries data from 2012-13 to 2019-20 to examine employment changes at firms covered by the law. They found that firms hired fewer women and more men after the amendment. The study found no significant change in firms’ output and profits. The effects were greater in industries that employed more women. In these industries, women employment fell 12%, while male employment rose 4.1%. Harshil Sharma, who holds a PhD in labour studies and has more than a decade of experience in labour welfare and policy reforms, said his fieldwork also showed similar barriers to women’s employment in construction. “PLFS [Periodic Labour Force Survey] data tells the same story: construction employs about 15.6% of India’s male workers but less than 5% of its women workers,” Sharma said. He said men had moved from agriculture into construction, while women’s share in the sector had remained flat. “On site, contractors avoid hiring women to sidestep obligations on separate toilets, maternity and safety, and to house more men in shared quarters,” he said. “Laws meant to empower women end up acting as a barrier to their entry.” The researchers recommended shifting maternity leave financing from individual employers to social insurance, introducing government-financed paternity leave and extending maternity protections to informal-sector workers. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Pallavi Singhal Pallavi Singhal covers agriculture, food policy and the rural economy from New Delhi. Over the past four years, she has reported extensively on farm policy, food inflation, procurement, agri-markets and rural livelihoods. Before joining Hindustan Times, she worked at Moneycontrol and Informist. A journalism post-graduate, she started as a trainee reporter in 2019 with The Indian Express, Chandigarh. news.headline: Reserve Bank of India Intensifies Oversight on Large Foreign Investments by Indian Firms
news.story_lead: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has escalated its regulatory scrutiny on significant foreign investments made by domestic corporations. The measure is designed to monitor outward foreign direct investment flows and strengthen compliance under capital transaction frameworks.
news.full_article_text:
### Increased Monitoring of Foreign Direct Investments

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has stepped up its oversight mechanism regarding large-scale foreign direct investments executed by Indian businesses. This regulatory stance aims to ensure strict adherence to cross-border capital regulations and mitigate risks related to outward capital movement.

### Key Regulatory Objectives
* **Compliance Verification:** Ensuring that large outward remittances and offshore investments strictly comply with the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) framework.
* **Financial Stability:** Monitoring corporate leverage and exposure linked to overseas step-down subsidiaries and foreign entities.
* **Risk Management:** Mitigating potential risks arising from complex foreign investment structures and foreign currency exposures.
bullet_points: RBI has increased scrutiny over major overseas investments conducted by domestic corporate entities.
The step focuses on enforcing regulatory compliance for outward cross-border capital transactions.
Outward Foreign Direct Investment (OFDI) is governed under the provisions of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA).
Enhanced tracking ensures better visibility into offshore investment structures and capital utilization.
key_facts: Regulator involved: Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
Focus area: Scrutiny on large foreign investments (Outward FDI) by Indian corporations.
Governing legal framework: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.
important_dates: 2026-10-21: Report on RBI's enhanced scrutiny of corporate foreign investments.
exam_relevance: Prelims: Regulatory roles of RBI under FEMA 1999, Outward Foreign Direct Investment (OFDI) rules, and external capital controls.
Mains: GS Paper III (Indian Economy, Regulation of Financial Sector, and External Sector Capital Management).
news.upsc_analysis: Enhanced regulatory oversight by the RBI on corporate foreign investments balances the need for global corporate expansion with macroeconomic stability and capital flow tracking. Ensuring compliance under FEMA prevents round-tripping and unverified foreign financial liabilities.
causes: Need for enhanced vigilance over large outward cross-border capital transactions.
Prevention of foreign exchange misuse and unmonitored capital outflow risks.
impacts: Increased compliance diligence for Indian corporate entities planning overseas investments.
Greater transparency in outward foreign direct investment (OFDI) reporting.
challenges: Balancing rigorous regulatory checks with the ease of doing business for Indian multinationals expanding abroad.
government_steps: RBI strengthening administrative oversight and scrutiny mechanisms for large corporate foreign investments.
way_forward: Streamline reporting mechanisms to maintain transparency while minimizing compliance hurdles for genuine corporate global expansion.
news.mains_notes: The RBI's heightened vigilance on large corporate foreign investments underscores the balance between capital account management and international corporate integration. Understanding FEMA guidelines, OFDI norms, and financial stability measures forms a crucial component of Indian external sector analysis.
mains_questions: Discuss the regulatory framework governing Outward Foreign Direct Investment (OFDI) in India. How does enhanced regulatory scrutiny by the RBI impact corporate expansion and financial stability?
Examine the role of the Reserve Bank of India in managing capital flows under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.

prelims_facts: RBI regulates Outward Foreign Direct Investment (OFDI) under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999.
Established in 1935, RBI serves as the primary regulator for foreign exchange and cross-border capital flows in India.

hindi_translation.headline: भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक ने कंपनियों के बड़े विदेशी निवेशों पर निगरानी बढ़ाई
hindi_translation.story_lead: भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (RBI) ने भारतीय कंपनियों द्वारा किए जाने वाले बड़े विदेशी निवेशों पर अपनी विनियामक निगरानी तेज कर दी है। इस कदम का उद्देश्य सीमा पार पूंजी प्रवाह की निगरानी करना और नियमों का पालन सुनिश्चित करना है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश की बढ़ती निगरानी

भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (RBI) ने भारतीय व्यवसायों द्वारा किए जाने वाले बड़े पैमाने के विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश (OFDI) के संबंध में अपनी जांच प्रक्रिया को कड़ा कर दिया है। इस विनियामक रुख का उद्देश्य विदेशी मुद्रा प्रबंधन अधिनियम (FEMA) के तहत सीमा पार पूंजी नियमों का कड़ाई से पालन सुनिश्चित करना है।

### प्रमुख विनियामक उद्देश्य
* **अनुपालन सत्यापन:** यह सुनिश्चित करना कि विदेश में धन भेजने और निवेश करने की प्रक्रियाएं कानूनी ढांचे के अनुरूप हों।
* **वित्तीय स्थिरता:** विदेशी सहायक कंपनियों और विदेशी संस्थाओं से जुड़े कॉर्पोरेट जोखिमों पर नज़र रखना।
* **जोखिम प्रबंधन:** जटिल विदेशी निवेश संरचनाओं से उत्पन्न होने वाले संभावित वित्तीय जोखिमों को कम करना।
bullet_points: RBI ने घरेलू कंपनियों द्वारा किए जाने वाले बड़े विदेशी निवेशों की जांच बढ़ा दी है।
इस कदम का मुख्य उद्देश्य सीमा पार पूंजी लेनदेन में विनियामक अनुपालन को मजबूत करना है।

news.headline: ‘Unpaid dues can’t be classified as savings': DMK leader lashes out at Vijay's TVK govt over debt claims
news.story_lead: ‘Unpaid dues can’t be classified as savings': DMK leader lashes out at Vijay's TVK govt over debt claims DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement. Former Tamil Nadu finance minister and DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay's TVK government over its claim of lowering debt as he accused it of deliberately stalling development works. He alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement.
news.full_article_text: ‘Unpaid dues can’t be classified as savings': DMK leader lashes out at Vijay's TVK govt over debt claims DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement. Former Tamil Nadu finance minister and DMK leader Thangam Thennarasu questioned chief minister C Joseph Vijay's TVK government over its claim of lowering debt as he accused it of deliberately stalling development works. He alleged that contractor payments are being withheld to falsely project a reduced debt burden as a financial achievement. He made the remarks in response to reports that Tamil Nadu's borrowing through government bonds fell by 21% in the first half of the current fiscal year compared to the corresponding period last year. Thennarasu questioned the government, which came in power in April this year, over its silence on underlying economic realities. Also read: PM Modi attends Delhi Dussehra celebration, calls Ramlila the 'end of tyranny, terror' He said the TVK government is trying to present lower borrowing as a ‘massive achievement’. "But shouldn't they disclose how this debt requirement decreased? They must release full details of the capital expenditure and developmental works undertaken in this first half," Thennarasu said in a post on X. As he made contrast between with the previous DMK government's performance, Thennarasu highlighted allocation figures from the 2025–26 budget. "Under the DMK governance, ₹ 57,231 crore was allocated for capital expenditures. According to provisional monthly accounts of the CAG, ₹ 13,002.22 crore was spent effectively between April and September 2025 on key infrastructure projects, including the Metro Rail," he noted. Also read: Model Shraddha Dubey, sister and driver arrested in Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma's death case He raised several questions and demanded to know what the exact capital expenditure incurred by the TVK government was from April to September. "Can a government claim financial management accolades by delaying development works, withholding payments for completed projects, and artificially inflating cash reserves to borrow less," Thennarasu asked, adding, "Keeping pending dues unpaid cannot be classified as savings." Also, he pointed out a massive contradiction in the government's fiscal roadmap, revealing that while the TVK administration boasts of reduced borrowing in the first half, it has planned a massive borrowing spree of ₹ 48,000 crore for the October–December quarter alone. This figure is more than double the ₹ 23,500 crore raised in the preceding quarter. Also read: CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka move Delhi HC against 2-day extension of judicial custody While claiming that borrowings declined in the first half of the financial year, the TVK government has planned to borrow ₹ 48,000 crore in the October–December quarter alone. Is this not more than double the ₹ 23,500 crore borrowed in the previous quarter? He alleged that the decline in borrowings is because the TVK government is ‘struggling to undertake capital expenditure’ amid revenue collections that remain below the estimates projected in its budget. “Tenders worth tens of thousands of crores of rupees have been cancelled. Roads are in poor condition due to the lack of development works, construction projects remain incomplete, and thousands of people have lost their jobs,” he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. In the meantime, she thought it was a good idea to share what she learnt, hence took up part-time teaching of journalism course at Jamia Millia Islamia, which she says, she thoroughly enjoyed-not sure if the feeling was mutual. For a year, she also tried her hands at communication roles, only to realise she was more comfortable with news. So, joined HT in September 2025. Not much of a talker, always up for chai and sarcasm. And pun always intended. Her tag line is 'I will figure out, but I need to panic first' Read More

news.headline: Vijay govt faces BJP ire over parole to Coimbatore blast convicts: 'Justice can't be compromised for politics'
news.story_lead: Vijay govt faces BJP ire over parole to Coimbatore blast convicts: 'Justice can't be compromised for politics' Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead. The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to grant 60 days' parole to five life convicts of the 1998 Coimbatore serial bomb blasts case has received backlash from the BJP and triggered a row in the state. Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead and a betrayal of the living.
news.full_article_text: Vijay govt faces BJP ire over parole to Coimbatore blast convicts: 'Justice can't be compromised for politics' Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead. The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to grant 60 days' parole to five life convicts of the 1998 Coimbatore serial bomb blasts case has received backlash from the BJP and triggered a row in the state. Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead and a betrayal of the living. He added that the decision shows the government’s “one-sided lenient approach” towards convicted terrorists. In a post on X, Thirupathy said, “Granting long-term parole to those involved in the bombing incident that shattered many families is not only an insult to the memory of those who lost their lives but also a grave betrayal to the survivors.” “It sends the wrong message to the people of Tamil Nadu that those who wage war against society can also be shown mercy. Before the brutality of this terrorist attack, which is considered one of the darkest chapters in the state's history, personal reasons can never take precedence,” he added. Also Read: ‘Unpaid dues can’t be classified as savings': DMK leader lashes out at Vijay's TVK govt over debt claims He added that BJP insists the revocation of the parole order immediately and hopes that no concessions are granted to convicts involved in this case. “The Bharatiya Janata Party insists that this 60-day parole order be revoked immediately and that no further concessions of any kind be granted to the 'Al-Umma' convicts involved in this case.” The BJP leader stressed that the terrorists must fully serve the sentences imposed on them as he said, “Justice for those affected by the Coimbatore bombing incident can never be compromised for political self-interest. Terrorists must fully serve the sentences imposed on them.” Also Read: Vijay’s TVK joins INDIA bloc protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for the first time What happened in Coimbatore bomb blasts case As many as 58 persons were killed and 250 had suffered injuries when 19 bomb explosions rocked Coimbatore city in Tamil Nadu between February 14 and 17, 1998. The improvised explosive devices, with time delay mechanisms, had been placed in cars, two-wheelers, abandoned bags, push carts, tea cans and so on. SA Basha and Mohammed Ansari, leaders of Muslim militant organisation Al-Umma, were the prime convicts in the case. “Mohammed Ansari, Mohammed Ali, Monappa alias Mohammed Hasan, Mohammed Azam, and Nawab Khan were convicted as guilty. Planned and executed by the banned 'Al-Umma' terrorist organization ahead of an election campaign rally, this attack was a brutal massacre against innocent people. The Supreme Court itself described this act as "most heinous" and refused to grant bail to these convicts,” Thirupathy said on X. Of the 166 accused in the case, the trial court in August 2007 pronounced 69 persons guilty of different offences. In December 2009, the Madras high court upheld the convictions of 18 people – 17 life terms and one 13-year term – in the case. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. She enjoys covering national and global news, focusing on delivering updates quickly and clearly so readers can make sense of what’s happening as it unfolds. Comfortable in high-pressure newsroom settings, she regularly contributes to live blogs, explainers and real-time coverage. Before joining Hindustan Times, she was part of the digital team at The Indian Express, worked with the social media team at Firstpost, and spent time as a creative strategist at Clematis Advertising. Outside of work, she likes exploring different art forms and unwinds with music. The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to grant 60 days' parole to five life convicts of the 1998 Coimbatore serial bomb blasts case has received backlash from the BJP and triggered a row in the state. Tamil Nadu BJP's chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy said that granting parole to men who helped plant bombs that tore apart families is an insult to the dead and a betrayal of the living. He added that the decision shows the government’s “one-sided lenient approach” towards convicted terrorists. In a post on X, Thirupathy said, “Granting long-term parole to those involved in the bombing incident that shattered many families is not only an insult to the memory of those who lost their lives but also a grave betrayal to the survivors.” “It sends the wrong message to the people of Tamil Nadu that those who wage war against society can also be shown mercy. Before the brutality of this terrorist attack, which is considered one of the darkest chapters in the state's history, personal reasons can never take precedence,” he added. Terrorists must fully serve the sentences imposed on them.” Also Read: Vijay’s TVK joins INDIA bloc protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for the first time What happened in Coimbatore bomb blasts case As many as 58 persons were killed and 250 had suffered injuries when 19 bomb explosions rocked Coimbatore city in Tamil Nadu between February 14 and 17, 1998. The improvised explosive devices, with time delay mechanisms, had been placed in cars, two-wheelers, abandoned bags, push carts, tea cans and so on. SA Basha and Mohammed Ansari, leaders of Muslim militant organisation Al-Umma, were the prime convicts in the case. “Mohammed Ansari, Mohammed Ali, Monappa alias Mohammed Hasan, Mohammed Azam, and Nawab Khan were convicted as guilty. Planned and executed by the banned 'Al-Umma' terrorist organization ahead of an election campaign rally, this attack was a brutal massacre against innocent people. The Supreme Court itself described this act as "most heinous" and refused to grant bail to these convicts,” Thirupathy said on X. Of the 166 accused in the case, the trial court in August 2007 pronounced 69 persons guilty of different offences. news.headline: ‘Kolkata pandal collapse claim unfounded’: Cops hunt for person behind rumour that led to stampede
news.story_lead: ‘Kolkata pandal collapse claim unfounded’: Cops hunt for person behind rumour that led to stampede The investigators are examining the CCTV footages to build the sequence of events that led to stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday. Over three days after 19 people were killed in Kolkata pandal stampede, the police are reportedly looking for a person who had allegedly misled revellers by announcing that a section of the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal was collapsing. The announcement reportedly triggered panic and led to the stampede on Saturday evening.
news.full_article_text: ‘Kolkata pandal collapse claim unfounded’: Cops hunt for person behind rumour that led to stampede The investigators are examining the CCTV footages to build the sequence of events that led to stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday. Over three days after 19 people were killed in Kolkata pandal stampede, the police are reportedly looking for a person who had allegedly misled revellers by announcing that a section of the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal was collapsing. The announcement reportedly triggered panic and led to the stampede on Saturday evening. The police have not found evidence to substantiate the claim, news agency PTI quoted the police as saying. "At present, there is no evidence to suggest that any part of the pandal was in a position to collapse," the police officer said. The investigators are examining CCTV footage to establish the sequence of events, police said. Thirty cameras are installed across the premises, footage from 13 covers the area where the incident took place, according to the police. Deep Dive Police said the analysis indicates that rain caused the exit point to be congested, while the entry point remained open despite the presence of a large crowd inside the pandal. A stampede situation took place at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening, killing 19 and leaving 25 injured. The investigators are analysing the CCTV footage to reconstruct the crowd's movement and determine how the situation escalated, the officer said, adding that the circumstances under which entry was allowed despite congestion at the exit may also come under scrutiny. Police said that there are key questions as to who made the announcement and what was the purpose. The announcement that a section of the structure was collapsing allegedly triggered panic among visitors. "Police have not found evidence to substantiate the claim," the officer said. The mic announcement warning of a possible structural collapse is believed to be one of the reasons that led to crowd crush at the Kolkata pandal. According to the police, the announcement – “The condition of the pandal is very bad. It will collapse. Please leave” – was made inside the pandal as the crowd jostled through a narrow bylane on Saptami, the seventh day of the festival, while rain lashed the city and left the streets slippery. The announcement was also mentioned by chief minister Suvendu Adhikari as he said, "Preliminary investigation has revealed that it was an announcement by the organisers which led to the stampede-like situation and resulted in so many deaths.” Seven people – mostly the pandal organisers – have been arrested so far in connection with the stampede that occurred around 7.30pm at Chorbagan, one of the city’s most popular Durga Puja venues, in cramped north Kolkata. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. In the meantime, she thought it was a good idea to share what she learnt, hence took up part-time teaching of journalism course at Jamia Millia Islamia, which she says, she thoroughly enjoyed-not sure if the feeling was mutual. For a year, she also tried her hands at communication roles, only to realise she was more comfortable with news. So, joined HT in September 2025. Not much of a talker, always up for chai and sarcasm. And pun always intended. Her tag line is 'I will figure out, but I need to panic first' Read More

news.headline: ‘Right to defend ourselves’: Jaishankar says India expects partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism
news.story_lead: ‘Right to defend ourselves’: Jaishankar says India expects partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism S Jaishankar earlier held a meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is on a three-day visit to India. External affairs minister S Jaishankar said in Mumbai on Tuesday that India expects its partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism as he thanked the US administration under President Donald Trump for extraditing 26/11 attack mastermind Tahawwur Hussain Rana. Track live updates on day 1 of Rubio's India visit “We are clear on the right to defend ourselves against terrorism and expect our partners show zero tolerance towards terrorism,” Jaishankar said, making an indirect reference to US ties with Pakistan, which is accused of harbouring terrorists and plotting against India.
news.full_article_text: ‘Right to defend ourselves’: Jaishankar says India expects partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism S Jaishankar earlier held a meeting with US secretary of state Marco Rubio, who is on a three-day visit to India. External affairs minister S Jaishankar said in Mumbai on Tuesday that India expects its partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism as he thanked the US administration under President Donald Trump for extraditing 26/11 attack mastermind Tahawwur Hussain Rana. Track live updates on day 1 of Rubio's India visit “We are clear on the right to defend ourselves against terrorism and expect our partners show zero tolerance towards terrorism,” Jaishankar said, making an indirect reference to US ties with Pakistan, which is accused of harbouring terrorists and plotting against India. Jaishankar made the remarks – during his address on American Independence Day celebration event in Mumbai – as he mentioned the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks, often called 26/11 attacks, in which coordinated shooting and bombing attacks took place across the city over four days, from November 26 to 29. At least 175 people died in the attacks and over 300 were injured in one of the worst terror attacks in India. The attack was carried out by Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), a Pakistan-based terror outfit. Rubio's India visit Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday for a three-day visit. Rubio and Jaishankar met earlier in the day where the leaders, along with UAE's foreign minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, where the leaders discussed regional energy security and way ahead on shared economic priorities. Jaishankar hosted Rubio for wide-ranging talks shortly after the top diplomat arrived in Mumbai for his second visit to India in under five months, even as bilateral ties remain strained over Washington's unpredictable trade policies and tightening immigration rules. Ahead of the meeting, the US Secretary of State described India as a crude oil refining "superpower" and advocated for processing more Venezuelan crude in India. The US Secretary of State is scheduled to visit Reliance Industries Ltd-owned Jamnagar Refinery on Wednesday. Rubio, answering a question on the proposed India-US trade pact, said "a small number of items" are left to be wrapped up and hoped that it will be sealed "shortly". "I would say we're about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So I think that will happen shortly -- we're hoping, which it should -- and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon. And perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter," he said. Following the meeting, Jaishankar said on social media that he and Rubio "shared views on further advancement of our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties." The US State Department said the secretary and the external affairs minister discussed regional and global issues, including developments in West Asia. "The secretary reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India's supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand," it said. news.headline: Rubio hails New Delhi as 'powerful, influential', says India-US ties will help shape 21st century
news.story_lead: Rubio hails New Delhi as 'powerful, influential', says India-US ties will help shape 21st century Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday and is scheduled to travel to Gujarat to visit Reliance's Jamnagar refinery on Wednesday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday hailed India as a "powerful, influential" nation, and said that India-US ties will define the 21st century. Rubio is on a three-day visit to India to hold talks over trade and energy ties among other issues of bilateral interest.
news.full_article_text: Rubio hails New Delhi as 'powerful, influential', says India-US ties will help shape 21st century Rubio arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday and is scheduled to travel to Gujarat to visit Reliance's Jamnagar refinery on Wednesday. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday hailed India as a "powerful, influential" nation, and said that India-US ties will define the 21st century. Rubio is on a three-day visit to India to hold talks over trade and energy ties among other issues of bilateral interest. The US Secretary of State arrived in India for the second time in less than five months. Speaking at the ‘Freedom 250 Reception’ in Mumbai, Rubio said, “It is a great honour to be back here today. At the press conference today, somebody asked a question, why are you back in India after just four months? And I said, well, number one, it happens to be the most populous nation on Earth. It happens to be the oldest democracy on Earth. It happens to be such a strong geopolitical partner.” The visit came amid lingering tensions between the two countries over several issues, including the Trump administration’s trade policies, immigration restrictions, and Washington’s growing engagement with Pakistan’s military leadership. India-US ties defining for 21st century: Rubio Rubio said he believes the relationship between the US and India will define what 21st century can look like. “If you think about the story and the history of the 21st century, it's being written in this region. And it's being written right now. One day someone will write a book about the history of the 21st century. And there will be a chapter in there about other regions in the world. But the 21st century will be defined for better and for worse by what happens in this region. We know that,” he said. “I truly believe the relationship between the United States and India is defining in many ways, in a positive way, what the 21st century can look like. Now, just to prove to you that those are not idle words.” Alignment between US-India extraordinary: Rubio Rubio backed his assertion citing the growing alignment on core issues between the two large countries. He said the alignment between India and the United States is particularly important given their size and global influence. “When you're talking about a country that's approximating 1.5 billion people, and the largest economy in the world in the United States, when two powers like that can be aligned on these issues that are going to define the 21st century, then we have an opportunity together to write those pages in the history of the 21st century,” he said. Speaking about geopolitics, Rubio cited the need to have a "free and open" Indo-Pacific where no nation can claim dominance or ownership on international shipping as among the core issues of alignment. “And in particular for the United States and India, a free and secure Indo-Pacific. On that, one in which no nation can claim dominance or ownership of international shipping lanes. On that issue, we are 100% and perfectly aligned,” said Rubio. He acknowledged that disagreements between nations are inevitable, stressing that what matters is a shared understanding on core issues. Rubio said the alignment between New Delhi and Washington on issues central to their respective national interests is “extraordinary.” "I could go on and on, but the point is, of course, no two nations on earth will ever be perfectly aligned on every issue. And of course, there will be times and points of disagreement. But on the core issues that matter, the core issues that define the national interest of both India and the United States, the alignment between our countries is extraordinary." We don't come enough: Rubio Sharing his interaction with a reporter earlier during a press conference, who asked Rubio why he was back in India just four months after his previous visit, Rubio quipped that he does not visit the country as often as he should, drawing a laughter. “And I'm glad to be back. I said earlier today we had this press conference. We had members of the media there, obviously. And they were asking, somebody asked a question, why are you back in India after just four months? I actually think we don't come enough. I actually think we don't come enough. And it's not just for the parties," he said. The Opposition leaders said that the CM left for a foreign tour at a time when the state was facing a grave drug crisis. Launching a sharp attack on the state government, BJP MP Tarun Chugh slammed CM Mann's visit to France, alleging that the Chief Minister opted to travel abroad with his wife to celebrate his birthday at a time when all of Punjab is engulfed in a crisis. "Due to the incompetence of the Aam Aadmi Party government led by Bhagwant Mann, the monster of drug abuse is devouring the youth of Punjab. Every day, in streets and villages, lives are being lost to drugs. Those who dare to oppose the drug menace are being murdered in broad daylight in public markets," he said. "Punjab is burning in the fire of drug addiction; law and order have completely collapsed...23 police stations have been targeted in grenade attacks, and even police personnel feel unsafe while in uniform," he added. Targeting the AAP government the BJP leader further stated, "At a time when all of Punjab is engulfed in a raging crisis, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has chosen to travel to France with his wife to celebrate his birthday. This is a deeply distressing situation. If this is an official state visit, how is his wife accompanying him? In reality, a birthday party is being hosted in France under the guise of an official state visit..." Meanwhile, former Union minister and BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu posted on X, "Paris Official Visit or Birthday Vacation? Bhagwant Mann’s birthday trip to Paris—in whose name, and at whose expense?" "Family in the delegation: Who is paying for his wife’s travel and stay—Punjab’s taxpayers," the leader added. Questioning about the invitation from France, he added, "Where is France’s invitation? The invitation is reportedly for MARKFED to participate in SIAL. Why does the CM need to fly to Paris?" "Punjab’s treasury is not a family holiday fund! Bhagwant Mann must disclose the purpose, expenses and official invitation. news.full_article_text: Rubio urges India to boost US energy, defence purchases in talks with Jaishankar Rubio noted that Indian companies can play a role in refining Venezuelan heavy crude as more of it enters the world market. India and the United States on Tuesday reviewed their bilateral cooperation, with the focus on energy and defence, as US secretary of state Marco Rubio used a meeting with external affairs minister S Jaishankar to urge the Indian side to increase energy trade and step up purchases of American technologies and systems. Jaishankar and Rubio, who travelled to India for the second time in less than five months with a large business delegation, met in the country’s financial hub against the backdrop of persisting strains in bilateral ties over a range of issues, including the Trump administration’s unpredictable trade policies, enhanced immigration restrictions affecting Indian professionals and the US’s growing proximity to Pakistan’s military leadership. Follow live updates on Marco Rubio's visit to India here . EAM Jaishankar on meeting with Rubio Deep Dive After the meeting with Rubio, Jaishankar said on social media that they discussed ways to further advance “our ties, focusing on trade, energy, technology, defence and people-to-people ties”, and exchanged views on regional developments. Rubio said in a separate social media post that they “discussed energy security and defence cooperation while reaffirming the importance of advancing the US-India strategic partnership”. Also Read | Rubio calls India ‘powerful, influential’, says India-US ties will define 21st century Purchases of American energy According to a readout from the US state department spokesman, Rubio pushed the Indian side to increase purchases of American energy, technologies and military and nuclear equipment. Rubio “reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India’s supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand," the readout said. Rubio commended progress in bilateral defence and civil nuclear cooperation, and “advocated for the increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both our countries”. There was no immediate response from Indian officials on Rubio’s comments. This was largely in line with the push from Washington during President Donald Trump’s second term for New Delhi to buy more energy, technology and military gear from the US. While India has diversified its energy sources over the past year, Russia remains the single largest source, accounting for more than 50% of all crude purchases, while the US was in third place with 5.1% in August. During a media interaction, Rubio described India as an important commercial and business partner of the US, a key member of the Quad and a strong strategic partner, and noted there is a “lot of defence cooperation” between the two sides. He also said the two sides are “very, very close” to finalising a bilateral trade deal. “I would say we’re about as close as you can be without having an executed agreement. I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So I think that will happen shortly – we're hoping, which it should – and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon. And perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter,” he said. A visit to the Reliance Industries-owned Jamnagar Refinery – currently the world’s largest with an installed capacity of 1.4 million barrels a day – is on Rubio’s itinerary for Wednesday, and he spoke extensively about the role of both India as a “refining superpower” and the Indian conglomerate in addressing global energy issues. Also Read | Rubio backs 'India's need to diversify' energy sources, says US can help meet needs amid Russian oil debate Rubio on energy supplies Rubio told the media that the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi attacks on energy pipelines in Saudi Arabia and attacks on refining facilities as part of the Russia-Ukraine conflict have impacted energy supplies, causing several countries to grapple with a diesel shortage. Days before Rubio’s arrival in India, President Donald Trump waived sweeping new sanctions under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act and announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to release hundreds of thousands of tonnes of Russian diesel onto the world market. Rubio noted that Indian companies can play a role in refining Venezuelan heavy crude as more of it enters the world market, an issue he planned to discuss during the visit to the Reliance refinery. “They have the capability to refine heavy crude, they have done so in the past. And I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do,” he said. “Refining capability is a key part of it and India is a refining superpower. They have the ability to do that and they have companies that know how to do that.” He also noted that Indian companies have pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela and can play a role in energy production. “With India, we've talked about it in the past…They're ready to do it, they're willing to do it. There might be a few impediments that stand in the way in terms of [pre-existing] sanctions,” he said. Asked about the reasons for his visit to the Reliance facility, Rubio replied: “Energy is related to national security. Countries fight wars over energy, economies collapse over lack of energy. We’re going to go see a company that has a tremendous amount of refining capability. It makes all the sense in the world to talk to them about it.” Rubio on India's steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy Rubio responded to another question about US satisfaction with India's steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy by noting that New Delhi has repeatedly expressed its desire to diversify its energy portfolio and that the US can be an energy source. “Obviously, it’s not easy to do that from one day to the next. I think they've made substantial progress in that regard, and we're happy to see that,” he said. “But in the end, it's not just about Russian oil; it's about their desire to diversify, and obviously we think we can be a source of some of their energy inputs. Obviously, we've discussed Venezuela and other countries, and I think it's in our interest to have a strong ally with a diverse energy portfolio,” Rubio said. Jaishankar and Rubio, who travelled to India for the second time in less than five months with a large business delegation, met in the country’s financial hub against the backdrop of persisting strains in bilateral ties over a range of issues, including the Trump administration’s unpredictable trade policies, enhanced immigration restrictions affecting Indian professionals and the US’s growing proximity to Pakistan’s military leadership.
