Rubio said in a separate social media post that they “discussed energy security and defence cooperation while reaffirming the importance of advancing the US-India strategic partnership”. Also Read | Rubio calls India ‘powerful, influential’, says India-US ties will define 21st century Purchases of American energy According to a readout from the US state department spokesman, Rubio pushed the Indian side to increase purchases of American energy, technologies and military and nuclear equipment. Rubio “reiterated that increased energy trade with the United States can play a transformative role in diversifying India’s supply chains while meeting its sizable consumer demand," the readout said. Rubio commended progress in bilateral defence and civil nuclear cooperation, and “advocated for the increased purchase of US technologies and systems, which can enhance the security and prosperity of both our countries”. There was no immediate response from Indian officials on Rubio’s comments. This was largely in line with the push from Washington during President Donald Trump’s second term for New Delhi to buy more energy, technology and military gear from the US. I think there's a small number of items left to wrap up. So I think that will happen shortly – we're hoping, which it should – and hopefully have some good news to announce fairly soon. And perhaps the leaders can sign it thereafter,” he said. A visit to the Reliance Industries-owned Jamnagar Refinery – currently the world’s largest with an installed capacity of 1.4 million barrels a day – is on Rubio’s itinerary for Wednesday, and he spoke extensively about the role of both India as a “refining superpower” and the Indian conglomerate in addressing global energy issues. And I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do,” he said. “Refining capability is a key part of it and India is a refining superpower. They have the ability to do that and they have companies that know how to do that.” He also noted that Indian companies have pre-existing oil concessions in Venezuela and can play a role in energy production. “With India, we've talked about it in the past…They're ready to do it, they're willing to do it. There might be a few impediments that stand in the way in terms of [pre-existing] sanctions,” he said. Asked about the reasons for his visit to the Reliance facility, Rubio replied: “Energy is related to national security. Countries fight wars over energy, economies collapse over lack of energy. We’re going to go see a company that has a tremendous amount of refining capability. It makes all the sense in the world to talk to them about it.” Rubio on India's steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy Rubio responded to another question about US satisfaction with India's steps to reduce dependence on Russian energy by noting that New Delhi has repeatedly expressed its desire to diversify its energy portfolio and that the US can be an energy source. “Obviously, it’s not easy to do that from one day to the next. news.headline: Lucknow murder: Shiva Sharma's mother welcomes Shraddha Dubey's arrest, claims 'videos of harassment' exist
news.story_lead: Lucknow murder: Shiva Sharma's mother welcomes Shraddha Dubey's arrest, claims 'videos of harassment' exist The arrests coincided with Vijayadashami, she said, expressing confidence that the case would proceed according to the due process of law. The mother of Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma, who died after falling off the balcony of an apartment building earlier this month, welcomed the arrest of three absconding accused in the case. Ranjana Sharma, mother of the victim, described the arrest of model Shraddha Dubey as the “first step toward justice” and thanked the Uttar Pradesh Police, Special Task Force (STF) and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for their efforts.
news.full_article_text: Lucknow murder: Shiva Sharma's mother welcomes Shraddha Dubey's arrest, claims 'videos of harassment' exist The arrests coincided with Vijayadashami, she said, expressing confidence that the case would proceed according to the due process of law. The mother of Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma, who died after falling off the balcony of an apartment building earlier this month, welcomed the arrest of three absconding accused in the case. Ranjana Sharma, mother of the victim, described the arrest of model Shraddha Dubey as the “first step toward justice” and thanked the Uttar Pradesh Police, Special Task Force (STF) and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for their efforts. Sharma's mother, who had lodged a murder complaint against Dubey and others, claimed that there was proof that her son was harassed. "Following this arrest, the case will proceed according to the due process of law. As for the harassment, there are many other videos currently in people's possession. I have full faith that justice will be served," she said. 28-year-old Shiva Sharma fell off the balcony of an apartment in the Balu Adda area of Hazratganj in Uttar Pradesh on October 9. Police on Tuesday arrested his alleged live-in partner Shraddha Dubey, her sister and their driver, who are the key accused in the case. They had been on the run since the day of the incident. Deep Dive Hailing the arrests, Shiva's mother said they coincided with Vijayadashami and expressed confidence that the case would proceed according to the due process of law. Also Read | Model Shraddha Dubey, sister and driver arrested in Lucknow cafe owner Shiva Sharma's death case Speaking to ANI, Ranjana Sharma said, “I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to everyone— the police, the STF, the administration, CM Yogi Adityanath, and all those who supported us. It is significant that today is the day of Vijayadashami, and this marks the first step toward justice for Shiva.” Arrest of three in Nagpur Prime suspect Shraddha Dubey, her sister Rashmi Dubey and driver Danish, who each carried a reward of ₹ 50,000, were arrested in Nagpur during a joint operation by the Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (UPSTF) and Lucknow Police, with assistance from Nagpur Police. Uttar Pradesh Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Amitabh Yash said Shraddha had evaded arrest by consistently wearing a burqa, minimising her use of communication devices, limiting interactions with others and staying in low-end hotels with minimal surveillance. "She will now be brought to Lucknow on transit remand, where the Lucknow Police will conduct interrogations and advance the investigation. To evade the police and remain on the run, she consistently wore a burqa, minimized the use of communication devices, and kept her interactions with others to an absolute minimum. She chose to stay in low-end hotels—places with minimal surveillance and less police oversight," he told reporters. Also Read | Hot pursuit, cold trail: Influencer still elusive in UP cafe owner's death, surrender possibility on the radar Shraddha travelled to Nepal to mislead investigators Yash also said police had received information that Shraddha had travelled to Nepal before returning, describing it as a possible attempt to mislead investigators. "This was likely an attempt to throw the police off her trail," he said. Speaking to ANI, the ADG said Shraddha was accompanied by her sister and driver, who had remained with her throughout the period she was absconding. Yash said Shraddha would be brought to Lucknow on transit remand, where the Lucknow Police would question her as part of the investigation. A murder case was registered at Hazratganj police station on October 9 under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), following a complaint by Ranjana Sharma. Lucknow Police had initially announced a reward of ₹ 25,000 for information leading to the accused, which was later increased to ₹ 50,000. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Priyanjali Narayan Priyanjali Narayan is a journalist with Hindustan Times based in New Delhi. news.headline: ‘Spend time with your families, remember Ashu, Saurav’: Abhijeet Dipke's emotional message to supporters ahead of festive season
news.story_lead: ‘Spend time with your families, remember Ashu, Saurav’: Abhijeet Dipke's emotional message to supporters ahead of festive season Abhijeet Dipke said that the consequences of the protests were also faced by their families of supporters and requested everyone to spend time with them. As Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka continue to be in jail, founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday made an emotional appeal to protestors and urged them to spend time with their families during the festive season. Dipke took to X as he thanked protestors for their support during past agitations and said that everyone had gone through a tough time during the protests.
news.full_article_text: ‘Spend time with your families, remember Ashu, Saurav’: Abhijeet Dipke's emotional message to supporters ahead of festive season Abhijeet Dipke said that the consequences of the protests were also faced by their families of supporters and requested everyone to spend time with them. As Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka continue to be in jail, founder Abhijeet Dipke on Tuesday made an emotional appeal to protestors and urged them to spend time with their families during the festive season. Dipke took to X as he thanked protestors for their support during past agitations and said that everyone had gone through a tough time during the protests. He added that the consequences were also faced by their families and requested everyone to spend time with them. “Hello cockroaches, how are you? I hope all of you are fine. I can see that for the past few days, all of you have been struggling really hard on the streets, in personal life, because of which we are putting up a fight. And I can understand what you are going through,” he said in a video message. Deep Dive Das and Ranka are lodged in Tihar Jail after they were arrested last week and sent to judicial custody for attempting to stage a protest at Jantar Mantar, which is now a de-notified protest cite. A Delhi magistrate court on Monday extended their judicial custody by two more days as it said the two CJP leaders ‘showed no respect for law’. "For a few days, spend time with your families. Be there with your families, be there with your loved ones," he said, adding, "Please remember Sourav and Ashu when you are with your families, because they both can't be with their families. So they are our family,” Dipke said in the social media post. news.headline: Uddhav Thackeray questions Tiger Shroff attack response, challenges Fadnavis to confront Bishnoi gang's leader
news.story_lead: Uddhav Thackeray questions Tiger Shroff attack response, challenges Fadnavis to confront Bishnoi gang's leader Targeting Fadnvis-led government, Thackeray said, “An attack took place on Tiger Shroff the other day. Did you rush to meet him immediately to gain publicity?” Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, addressing a Dussehra rally on Tuesday, criticised the Maharashtra government's response to the attack on actor Tiger Shroff. Three men opened fire at Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area on Sunday evening as he was leaving a football ground.
news.full_article_text: Uddhav Thackeray questions Tiger Shroff attack response, challenges Fadnavis to confront Bishnoi gang's leader Targeting Fadnvis-led government, Thackeray said, “An attack took place on Tiger Shroff the other day. Did you rush to meet him immediately to gain publicity?” Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, addressing a Dussehra rally on Tuesday, criticised the Maharashtra government's response to the attack on actor Tiger Shroff. Three men opened fire at Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area on Sunday evening as he was leaving a football ground. Targeting the chief minister Devendra Fadnavis-led state government, Thackeray said in the rally, “An attack took place on Tiger Shroff the other day. Did you rush to meet him immediately to gain publicity?” "But how did the attackers manage to bring weapons there in the first place? This is not an act worthy of a Shaurya Medal," news agency ANI quoted the leader as saying. Deep Dive Thackeray further alleged that the Bishnoi gang claims its network exceeds 70,000 members and challenged the chief minister to take on the gang leaders. "Had they been shot the moment they arrived, that would have been something worth acknowledging. The Bishnois are sitting around eating dhokla. Bishnoi's men claim that they have 70,000 people in their network. If Devendra Fadnavis has the courage, he should go to Delhi and tell their leader directly," Thackeray added. Also Read | Tiger Shroff's team releases first statement after attack, warns of legal action over AI-generated videos and fake claims Tiger Shroff shooting case In the incident, the actor escaped unhurt, his driver and another person were injured in the incident. Following the attack, the Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility, according to a viral social media post. However, police have yet to verify the claim, news agency PTI reported. Meanwhile, the three assailants who shot at Shroff were arrested from aboard a Jaipur-bound express train at Kota junction on Monday, a s HT reported earlier. Also Read | Mother of suspect in Tiger Shroff shooting case claims son was lured, trapped Tiger Shroff's team releases statement after attack The actor's team released a statement on Tuesday, warning against the spread of fake news and AI-generated content. "We would like to categorically clarify that Tiger Shroff has made no statements, released no videos, and authorised no communication regarding the recent incident or any related developments," the statement noted. "It has come to our attention that several social media pages and digital platforms are circulating fabricated stories, AI-generated videos, and scripted narratives, falsely attributed to Tiger. These are completely false, unauthorised, and intended to mislead the public We do not endorse, support, or have any association with such content," it read. The statement added, "We request everyone to rely only on verified communication from Tiger Shroff and his official team." Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, addressing a Dussehra rally on Tuesday, criticised the Maharashtra government's response to the attack on actor Tiger Shroff. Three men opened fire at Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area on Sunday evening as he was leaving a football ground.

Targeting the chief minister Devendra Fadnavis-led state government, Thackeray said in the rally, “An attack took place on Tiger Shroff the other day. Did you rush to meet him immediately to gain publicity?”
"But how did the attackers manage to bring weapons there in the first place? This is not an act worthy of a Shaurya Medal," news agency ANI quoted the leader as saying.
Thackeray further alleged that the Bishnoi gang claims its network exceeds 70,000 members and challenged the chief minister to take on the gang leaders.

Delhi Police Special Cell arrested four more accused on Tuesday in connection with the October 18 firing at actor Tiger Shroff’s car in Mumbai. Following the Delhi Police action, the four accused in the shooting case were formally arrested by the Mumbai Police's CID unit. The suspects were tracked down and caught from Kota in Rajasthan on Monday morning as they were planning to flee to Nepal. Following the arrest, the police said that the motive of the shooting was being ascertained, while the way Shroff was attacked, the assailants planned to kill him. news.headline: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family
news.story_lead: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family Anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh was shot dead inside a medical shop on October 13. His family reused to cremate his body till a CBI inquiry was ordered. Seven days have passed since Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, was shot dead inside a medical store at a busy market in Mansa.
news.full_article_text: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family Anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh was shot dead inside a medical shop on October 13. His family reused to cremate his body till a CBI inquiry was ordered. Seven days have passed since Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, was shot dead inside a medical store at a busy market in Mansa. However, he is yet to be cremated as his father, an ex-serviceman, Bhim Singh, had announced on October 13 that the family would not allow a post-mortem or conduct the last rites until the case is handed to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). But now Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has announced that the state government will hand over the probe into the murder case to the CBI. Jhota's murder on October 13 was livestreamed on Facebook. The Punjab government announcement came ahead of Union home minister Amit Shah's visit the family of Jhota and two other anti-drug activists killed in Punjab recently. Shah on Tuesday met the aggrieved families amid growing concerns over drug trafficking and law and order in Punjab. Deep Dive During his visit to Punjab, Shah went to the residence of late Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur to offer his condolences to the bereaved family. He also met with the family members of Gulzar Singh, who was killed for standing up against local chitta (synthetic drugs) peddlers in Sangrur. In a post shared on X, Shah expressed his grief, saying, "Today, at the residence of the family of late Bikramjit Singh ji, who lost his life for raising his voice against the unchecked drug trade in Punjab under the AAP government, I met them in Gurdaspur and expressed my condolences. May God grant them the strength to bear this sorrow." Amid Mann government's announcement of a CBI probe in Jhota's killing, Shah assured that the central agency will pursue the culprits involved in the killing regardless of their influence. “This morning, upon returning after celebrating his birthday, Bhagwant Mann Ji did one good thing—he handed over one inquiry to the CBI. I want to give my word to the people of Punjab: in the case handed over to us, whoever is found guilty—no matter how powerful or big they are—we will track them down even from the depths of the earth and hand them over to the law. We will bring them before the court,” Shah said in a dig at CM Mann, news agency PTI reported. "And today, I also want to appeal to the Chief Minister: you will not be able to handle it. Hand over the remaining two cases to the CBI as well. That is also the demand of their family members," he added. Shah said the ground reality described by the victims' families and residents was far more severe than what is captured in administrative files. "Meeting these three families, as well as the locals who were troubled and distressed by the chitta (drug) trade and had gathered at their homes—the reality of the situation in Punjab that they described turned out to be far more gut-wrenching and shattering than anything we read in official paper reports in Delhi," Shah said. Shah set a deadline of December 31, 2029, to eradicate the illicit narcotics network from Punjab, asserting that the Centre will track down and prosecute all perpetrators involved in the killings of anti-drug activists in the state. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sana Fazili Sana started her career in 2018 with News18 and later moved to BoomLive. In the meantime, she thought it was a good idea to share what she learnt, hence took up part-time teaching of journalism course at Jamia Millia Islamia, which she says, she thoroughly enjoyed-not sure if the feeling was mutual. For a year, she also tried her hands at communication roles, only to realise she was more comfortable with news. So, joined HT in September 2025. Not much of a talker, always up for chai and sarcasm. bullet_points: Punjab activist Jhota's kin refuse to cremate him; Amit Shah vows ‘drug-free’ state after meeting family
Anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh was shot dead inside a medical shop on October 13. His family reused to cremate his body till a CBI inquiry was ordered.

Seven days have passed since Punjab anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh, alias Jhota, was shot dead inside a medical store at a busy market in Mansa. However, he is yet to be cremated as his father, an ex-serviceman, Bhim Singh, had announced on October 13 that the family would not allow a post-mortem or conduct the last rites until the case is handed to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).

But now Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has announced that the state government will hand over the probe into the murder case to the CBI. Jhota's murder on October 13 was livestreamed on Facebook.

The Punjab government announcement came ahead of Union home minister Amit Shah's visit the family of Jhota and two other anti-drug activists killed in Punjab recently. Shah on Tuesday met the aggrieved families amid growing concerns over drug trafficking and law and order in Punjab.

During his visit to Punjab, Shah went to the residence of late Bikramjit Singh in Gurdaspur to offer his condolences to the bereaved family. He also met with the family members of Gulzar Singh, who was killed for standing up against local chitta (synthetic drugs) peddlers in Sangrur.

In a post shared on X, Shah expressed his grief, saying, "Today, at the residence of the family of late Bikramjit Singh ji, who lost his life for raising his voice against the unchecked drug trade in Punjab under the AAP government, I met them in Gurdaspur and expressed my condolences. May God grant them the strength to bear this sorrow."
Amid Mann government's announcement of a CBI probe in Jhota's killing, Shah assured that the central agency will pursue the culprits involved in the killing regardless of their influence.

news.story_lead: Students gather at Delhi's Model Town park to burn 20-feet tall ‘Gyanesh Kumar effigy’, detained Police said the students were occupying space in a park, burning an effigy and protesting after which they were briefly detained. Several students and activists associated with Krantikari Yuva Sangathan were detained by the police on Tuesday after they burned the effigy of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar during Dussehra celebrations near Delhi’s Model Town. Krantikari Yuva Sangathan is a Delhi-based independent student and youth organisation.
news.full_article_text: Students gather at Delhi's Model Town park to burn 20-feet tall ‘Gyanesh Kumar effigy’, detained Police said the students were occupying space in a park, burning an effigy and protesting after which they were briefly detained. Several students and activists associated with Krantikari Yuva Sangathan were detained by the police on Tuesday after they burned the effigy of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar during Dussehra celebrations near Delhi’s Model Town. Krantikari Yuva Sangathan is a Delhi-based independent student and youth organisation. The alleged effigy-burning took place at Sangam Park near Model Town in northwest Delhi where the KYS students erected a 20-feet tall effigy with a poster of Gyanesh Kumar and slogans such as “Sack Gyanesh Kumar”, “Loot-tantra” and “Discrimination, Injustice”. The student organisation had made the announcement about burning the effigy of Kumar alongside Ravana on Monday. On Tuesday, the group was joined by some locals to burn the effigy but were stopped by the police. Jyoti, a Delhi University student associated with KYS, told HT, “We are well within our rights to burn a Ravana effigy. Why are they trying to protect Gyanesh from everything? We just want to show our dissent. The police came in. We don’t know who called them or if they were tracking us. There was a tussle but we still managed to burn the effigy. After burning the effigy, the policemen got angry and pushed us. Many of the students managed to leave but some were detained” Mudiya, the national spokesperson of KYS said the programme was organised to highlight the issue of irregularities in SIR of electoral polls. “Several activists were illegally detained by the police after the programme. Effigy burning is a form of freedom of speech and expression that is a fundamental right. Numerous judgments by high courts and the Supreme Court have upheld effigy burning as a form of expression protected under Article 19 of the Constitution of India.” A senior police officer said the protesters had not taken any permission for the protest and were burning effigy near a residential colony. “We had only removed a few protesters and detained 10-12 people. They were released within a few hours” said an officer. As Dussehra is being celebrated and effigies of Ravana are being burnt at various spots in the country, organisers at Pitampura ground in Delhi made a 30-foot long cockroach effigy, a veiled attack at the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) which is under legal scrutiny amid its protests against the CEC over the alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls.

news.headline: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 73 security recruits, local authorities say
news.story_lead: Yemen's government said the missile strike killed recruits to its internal security forces (file photo) - Published 19 October 2026 More than 70 security personnel were killed in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa on Monday, local authorities say. The Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police. The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response".
news.full_article_text: Yemen's government said the missile strike killed recruits to its internal security forces (file photo) - Published 19 October 2026 More than 70 security personnel were killed in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa on Monday, local authorities say. The Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police. The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response". The Houthis' military spokesman said they had targeted "Saudi enemy concentrations". Yemen's devastating civil war has flared up in recent months. At the start of October, pro-government forces launched a major offensive that aims to retake territory in western Yemen that is controlled by the Houthis. With air support from a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states, they managed to regain control of territory on the Red Sea coast that overlooks the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, which the Houthis captured in a surprise assault in September. However, fierce fighting is continuing there, as well as around the besieged government-controlled city of Taiz, and to the north in Marib and al-Jawf provinces. The Houthis have also responded to the Saudi air strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in neighbouring Saudi Arabia. - Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says Published 4 days ago - On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged Published 12 October - 'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls Published 6 October Monday's attack in Shabwa was the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation. Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces. A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground at the camp. Hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and were forced to transfer the most seriously wounded people to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based, Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency. Shabwa's media office initially reported that 53 people were killed and 200 injured in the attack. But on Tuesday, it said in a new statement that Governor Awad bin al-Wazir had been informed by an investigative committee that the death toll was now 73, with another 14 individuals reported missing. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target. He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes". The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children. According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks. The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August. In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. Related topics
